thread:
maria: Heads up — apac-west egress NATs hit port exhaustion this morning around 08:12 UTC; ~3% of requests got routed to eu-west as failover. We're seeing 5xx spikes and increased latency for short-lived RPCs.

shiv: Yep. SNAT port usage hit 98% on natgw-02b. Dashboards: https://grafana/redwood/d/apac-egress — TCP TIME_WAIT pileup.

liam: Any link to the specific serving pool? Could this be the new batch of inference replicas?

maria: It correlates with a surge of short-lived connections from apac-gpu-pool-3 (many kv-cache misses after a rollout). Also saw some instance preemptions which caused ephemeral IP churn.

esther: Quick debug: grepped node kernels — lots of sockets in TIME_WAIT. Kernel ephemeral port range is default (32768-61000) on nodes. For high fanout we should tune `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` and `tcp_tw_reuse`.

ken: ops-bot: nat-health-check apac-west

ops-bot: [run] nat-health-check started for apac-west (job id: 2026-03-18-0730). Collecting SNAT port metrics, NAT gateway metrics, and conntrack stats.

maria: Two issues to solve: 1) immediate mitigation so we don't keep failing over; 2) longer term GeoDNS/failover policy change so short egress blips don't cause region flip.

shiv: For (2) I propose adding a probe smoothing window and a soft-eject path. Current GeoDNS config flips as soon as probe_count > 0, TTL 10s -> flip flops. Proposed: TTL 30s, probe_smoothing_window_ms: 120000, max_consecutive_failures: 3, soft_eject_traffic_pct: 10.

maria: +1. Short TTL makes things worse. If we increase TTL to 30s and require 3 failed probes across a 2min window we should avoid reacting to transient SNAT saturation.

liam: Soft-eject is interesting: route a small fraction to eu-west to warm caches rather than full roll. That reduces cold-cache tail when we do full failover. But it also means some extra cross-region egress bandwidth.

esther: For immediate fix: kernel tunings on node pool and ephemeral port widening. Commands we can run:
```bash
# widen ephemeral ports
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 65535"
# allow TIME_WAIT reuse
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
# reduce TIME_WAIT duration (careful)
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```
Apply via node-init daemonset for rollout.

ken: Another mitigation: assign additional SNAT IPs to egress NATs and adjust SNAT pool size on our egress proxies. On GCP we can add more IP aliases rather than spinning NAT gateways. Cheaper.

maria: Agreed — prefer scaling SNAT capacity before creating whole new NAT GW. Also autoscale SNAT pool based on port_utilization > 80% for 1m.

shiv: GeoDNS config snippet (proposal):
```yaml
geo_failover:
  probe_ttl_ms: 5000
  probe_smoothing_window_ms: 120000
  max_consecutive_failures: 3
  dns_ttl_secs: 30
  soft_eject_traffic_pct: 10
  fallback_policy: regional_priority
```
This keeps DNS changes rare and gives a soft path for traffic while the region recovers.

liam: Cost note: keeping standby SNATs and soft-eject cross-region traffic will add egress cost. Ballpark estimate: extra 2-5% egress + small NAT gateway charges — I'll model it.

esther: Runbook changes: add a section for snat_port_exhaustion with quick checks and `kubectl logs` commands + how to apply sysctl via daemonset. I'll draft.

maria: Action items:
- ken: roll kernel tweaks to apac-gpu-pool-3 and run synthetic ramp test (50k conns/min) — please do a canary first.
- shiv: patch GeoDNS with probe_smoothing_window_ms and dns_ttl_secs=30, add soft_eject path; run in staging.
- liam: estimate cost delta for soft-eject and extra SNAT capacity, include monthly and p95 scenarios.
- esther: write runbook and add troubleshooting checklist.

ken: I'll pick 1 + test. Canary target: 1 node set first, then 10%. ETA 2h.

shiv: I'll prepare the GeoDNS PR and run a dry run in staging. ETA 3h.

liam: I'll have cost numbers in 6h.

esther: I'll start the runbook and link to this thread.

maria: If this repeats we should consider a longer-term design change: egress proxy connection pooling + persistent upstreams to reduce ephemeral port churn. Worth tracking as backlog item.

ken: noted — created ticket INFRA-2189 for persistent egress proxies and SNAT pool autoscaling.

maria: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread for postmortem if recurrence > 1/week. :thumbsup:
